paragraphs.source_en: If young people in the society producing the Round Heads had undergone initiation, one possible testimony to this could be the Tin Tazarift shelter on the Tassili Plateau. The shelter is found inside a stone city and hidden by surrounding rocks, suggesting a secret character. The central part of the wall is dominated by seven roughly life-sized individuals, probably all male (some figures are partially eroded) and a female on the extreme left of the panel. It seems to be a composition in which two standing men with bows surround men without bows and depicted in horizontal positions (Fig. 5-8). The man on the extreme right seems to be the main figure towards which all others are oriented, except for the female which is turned to the other side.

The central part of the wall is dominated by seven roughly life-sized individuals, probably all male (some figures are partially eroded) and a female on the extreme left of the panel.
It seems to be a composition in which two standing men with bows surround men without bows and depicted in horizontal positions (Fig. 5-8).
The man on the extreme right seems to be the main figure towards which all others are oriented, except for the female which is turned to the other side.

paragraphs.source_en: He has some characteristic Round Head male attributes, such as the protuberances exiting from the top of the head, bulgy neck, a kind of pointed phallic pouch and an oval bracelet on the left arm.

paragraphs.source_en: Information can be gained from the figures themselves. Firstly, the difference between the men's attributes should be considered significant. The hunter on the right side and the "flying" men have protuberances on the heads but their number and shape are not identical; two long and rounded protuberances on the hunter's head compared to four short pointed projections on the uppermost "flying" man and two curved projections of the lower "flying" male. Secondly the bows and the phallic pouch are exclusive to the standing males. Thirdly the half-moon like object, the antelope and probably also the body decoration are only attributed to the upper horizontal figure.

units.source_en: Information can be gained from the figures themselves.
Firstly, the difference between the men's attributes should be considered significant.

The hunter on the right side and the "flying" men have protuberances on the heads but their number and shape are not identical; two long and rounded protuberances on the hunter's head compared to four short pointed projections on the uppermost "flying" man and two curved projections of the lower "flying" male.
Secondly the bows and the phallic pouch are exclusive to the standing males.
Thirdly the half-moon like object, the antelope and probably also the body decoration are only attributed to the upper horizontal figure.

paragraphs.source_en: This comparison suggests that the men represented are not equal in some way. They could have all been depicted in the same manner but they are deliberately different. Different attributes were probably not just decorative elements but they may stand for a different level or status within the society. We can therefore postulate that the figures represent individuals with unequal roles within the group. The ethnographic record indicates that the bow is a sign exclusive to post-initiation adult male hunters. The rite of passage in the San society occurs after the first large game kill, the most precious prey being an antelope, especially the eland (Silberbauer 1965; Lee 1979). Body paintings of the "new man" are an important part of the initiation in many African societies (Ten Raa 1969; Lee 1979; Le Quellec 2004).
